narrative: OMX30 faces a bullish correlation signal (+1.09%) led by Asian strength and broad-based commodity recovery, particularly copper (+5.0%) and gold (+3.4%). While the index trades +3.7% above its 200-MA in bull regime, technicals show caution: MACD below signal, ADX at 8.2 (weak), and RSI neutral at 48.83 suggest consolidation rather than breakout momentum. The 1.14% drop in US 10Y yields to 4.85% and VIX compression (-1.60%) support risk appetite, but ADX weakness reduces conviction. Watch 3,180 resistance (50-MA) and 3,085 support (lower Bollinger band); yesterday close at 3,123 is the pivot.
morningBrief: OMX30 opens with a bullish overnight backdrop: Shanghai +3.73%, Hang Seng +2.10%, and broad US strength (S&P +1.18%, NASDAQ +1.63%) set a risk-on tone. Copper's +5.0% surge is a major tail wind for Boliden and mining-linked industrials. USD/SEK at 10.26 (+0.30%) supports exporters like Volvo, Atlas Copco, and Ericsson despite NASDAQ strength. However, ADX at 8.2 is weak—reduce conviction by 30% and watch for consolidation. Key watch: 3,180 (50-MA resistance) and 3,085 (lower Bollinger) define the range. Banks get modest lift from yield normalization, but real estate stays under pressure. US Jobless Claims (14:30 CET) is the main event risk; any surprise could spike volatility. Play sectors: Industrials (cyclical beta), Mining (copper/gold tailwind), Banks (NIM relief). Avoid overextension into resistance.
